rationale: A wins, barely, because it keeps the dangerous credit story closer to the actual facts. Its strongest move is the proof demand for "how the program is capitalized (own balance sheet vs. a warehouse facility vs. an unnamed bank partner)," which is exactly the question a serious reporter asks. B is more structurally varied, especially with "Small brands on Faire now get paid before the retailer pays," but it dirties the work with "lender to 700,000 small retailers" before eligibility or usage is proven. That is how a decent angle gets turned into a correction request.
gaps_in_A: "Independent retailers say cash flow, not demand, is what keeps them from ordering" overstates the supplied fact. Faire says cash flow is the top barrier to ordering; the update does not prove demand is not a barrier.

"Faire, valued at $12.6B, quietly becomes a lender," "A wholesale marketplace becomes a bank," and "Someone is still paying for the risk" are all useful, but they crowd the same fintech-risk territory. One of them needs to be merged or clearly assigned to a different outlet lane.
"rather than routing through a named bank or BNPL partner" gets ahead of the evidence. The update says Faire underwrites using order history; it does not rule out a funding partner.
"A wholesale marketplace becomes a bank" is a little cute for the facts. It is a metaphor, not a confirmed regulatory or business-model status.
gaps_in_B: "Faire is quietly becoming a lender to 700,000 small retailers" is the big sin. The facts say Faire connects over 700,000 retailers; they do not say all are eligible, approved, or borrowing.
"using order history instead of traditional credit files" invents a contrast. The update says order history is used; it does not say traditional credit files are not used.
"crossing into balance-sheet finance" treats the funding source as settled while the same set later admits it needs proof on whether this sits on Faire's balance sheet, a debt facility, or a partner.
"brand-side payment terms change with it" and "Small brands" assume prior payment terms and brand size that are not in the update. The brand-side angle is good; the wording is not house-trained.
